title: 10 Best Cooking Classes in Rome
description: The 10 best cooking classes in Rome — handmade pasta, cacio e pepe, carbonara, pizza & full Roman menus. Real reviews, prices, neighborhoods & interactive map.

places.name: Eat & Walk Italy
places.whatToOrder: Book the '3 in 1' class — fettuccine, stuffed ravioli, and tiramisu in one session. The Pasta + Tiramisu with Wine class is the cheaper entry point if you only want one pasta shape.
places.insiderTip: Morning classes are calmer and the chefs have more bandwidth; evening sessions get loud and group-trip-y. They take dietary restrictions (vegetarian, gluten-free) with 24h notice and the meeting point is genuinely walkable from any centro storico hotel.
places.editorialSummary: The most-reviewed cooking class in Rome by a wide margin (nearly 11,000 TripAdvisor reviews at 4.9★) and the city's TripAdvisor Travelers' Choice winner five years running. It's hands-on with no pasta machines — you mix, roll, and shape every piece — and the venue is a real Roman restaurant (Gusto al Passetto) right next to Palazzo Altemps, two minutes from Piazza Navona. The price-to-quality ratio is the best in the centro storico.

redditQuotes.text: Voted best cooking class in Rome for 5 consecutive years and with over 20,000 five-star reviews — fresh pasta, pizza & tiramisù taught by a local chef in small groups with wine included.
redditQuotes.source: — Eat & Walk Italy, summarised from TripAdvisor Travelers' Choice 2021–2025 listings

redditQuotes.text: Eat & Walk offers a €55 pasta-and-tiramisu session that's described as a budget crowd-pleaser… 97% positive ratings from over 5,000 reviews, featuring fettuccine, stuffed ravioli, and quick tiramisu in an air-conditioned studio.
redditQuotes.source: — italyprivatetour.it 'Rome Cooking Classes 2025: Brutally Honest Reviews', posted 2025

places.name: InRome Cooking
places.neighborhood: Centro Storico (between Pantheon and Piazza Navona)
places.whatToOrder: The Pizza Masterclass (Roman thin-crust + a proper margherita) is what InRome is best known for, but the Roman Pastas class — cacio e pepe, carbonara, amatriciana or gricia — is the more useful one to take home.
places.insiderTip: If your dates are tight, book the second InRome school next to the Pantheon — same chefs, same recipes, often more availability than the flagship. Allergies and gluten-free are handled if you flag them at booking.
places.editorialSummary: InRome runs out of a 17th-century palazzo directly opposite Palazzo Madama (the Italian Senate), one of the prettiest cooking-class settings in the city. The chefs (Marco, Giulio, et al.) are full-time pros who teach pasta, pizza, gnocchi, and gelato across separately bookable shared classes — so you can pick the dish you actually want to learn instead of being railroaded into the standard fettuccine + tiramisu combo.

redditQuotes.text: InRome Cooking offers a €89 story-rich, small group lunch in a 17th-century palazzo… set opposite the Italian parliament and just around the corner from Piazza Navona.
redditQuotes.source: — italyprivatetour.it 'Rome Cooking Classes 2025: Brutally Honest Reviews', posted 2025

redditQuotes.text: Amazing cooking class with Chef Marco — he taught us how to cook two classic dishes of pasta and Tiramisu. The friendly chefs create a welcoming atmosphere that feels like family.
redditQuotes.source: — TripAdvisor review summary, InRome Cooking Classes (4.9★ · 877 reviews), 2025

places.name: Cooking Classes in Rome (with Chef Andrea Consoli)
places.whatToOrder: Tell Andrea in advance you want the Roman classics — carbonara or amatriciana for the pasta course, saltimbocca alla romana for the secondo, tiramisu for dessert. The seasonal vegetable antipasto is the part you'll actually use back home.
places.insiderTip: Andrea's wife Cinzia handles bookings and is excellent on email — write her directly through the site and ask for the morning slot if you want a less hurried experience. They accommodate gluten-free, vegetarian, and pescatarian with notice.
places.editorialSummary: If you only have one class to take in Rome and you actually want to learn how Romans cook, this is it. Chef Andrea Consoli runs hands-on, 4-hour private classes out of his Trastevere kitchen on Via dei Fienaroli, working from a fully seasonal menu (artichokes and zucchini blossoms in spring; porcini and chestnuts in autumn). You build a full antipasto-pasta-secondo-dolce meal from scratch and sit down with wine to eat it. 99% of reviewers recommend.

redditQuotes.text: He taught us some dishes including making pasta — appreciated his explanations of local versus tourist food and seasonal ingredients.
redditQuotes.source: — Jean, Rick Steves Italy travel forum, posted Mar 2025

redditQuotes.text: He is fun to cook with, interesting to learn from, and his food is unbelievably good… a masterful chef with endless knowledge and passion.
redditQuotes.source: — TripAdvisor review summary, Private Cooking Class with Chef Andrea Consoli (5.0★ · 144 reviews), 2025

places.name: Nonna's — Handmade Pasta with Grandma (Nonna Nerina)
places.neighborhood: Palombara Sabina (35 km / 30 min northeast of Rome)
places.address: Via del Plebiscito 4, 00018 Palombara Sabina RM
places.whatToOrder: The standard half-day workshop covers fettuccine, ravioli, and a regional shape (often cavatelli or strozzapreti). Email info@nonnas.it ahead if you want gluten-free dough — they do it well.
places.insiderTip: Take the early FL2 train from Roma Tiburtina and aim to be in Palombara by 10am. Bring cash for the village cafe afterwards. Kids 6+ are welcome and Nonna is exceptionally good with them.
places.editorialSummary: The original 'cooking with a real Italian nonna' experience and still the gold standard. Nonna Nerina taught the world to make pasta on Airbnb in 2019, and her family-run workshop in the medieval hilltop village of Palombara Sabina is rated 4.99★ on Airbnb across more than a thousand reviews. You hand-shape three different pasta types in her kitchen and eat them together at the family table. It's not 'cooking class as an activity' — it's a day in a Roman village.

redditQuotes.text: This is hands down the best day of the 3 weeks we spent in Italy… Do it!
redditQuotes.source: — TripAdvisor review, Nonna's Handmade Pasta with Grandma, posted Jun 2025

redditQuotes.text: Nonna Nerina's Sabina village workshop remains the gold standard — book four weeks out for weekend slots. You meet at Rome's Tiburtina station, hop on a regional train, and by 10 AM you're wrist‑deep in semolina in a medieval village kitchen.
redditQuotes.source: — italyprivatetour.it 'Rome Cooking Classes 2025: Brutally Honest Reviews', posted 2025

places.name: Riccardo Cooking Class (Rome Cooking Club)
places.whatToOrder: The Pasta Class & Sauces (€102) is the flagship — you make tonnarelli for cacio e pepe, fettuccine for ragù, and stuffed ravioli, plus four sauces from scratch. Add the wine pairing.
places.insiderTip: It's not in the centro storico — budget 25 minutes from the Pantheon by bus (Tram 8 to Trastevere then bus 75/H, or just take a taxi for ~€12). Worth it: prices and crowds are lower than dead-center classes.
places.editorialSummary: Ranked #7 of 362 cooking classes & workshops in Rome on TripAdvisor with a flat 5.0★ across 536 reviews — almost unheard of at that volume. Chef Riccardo runs both a pasta + sauces class (three pasta types, four sauces) and a separate pizza class with Aperol spritz built in, plus everything is paired with regional wines included in the price. A short tram or bus ride from Trastevere puts you in a residential area where you actually eat with locals afterwards.

redditQuotes.text: An absolutely brilliant experience. The pasta tasted incredible and the instructors were excellent hosts and chefs.
redditQuotes.source: — TripAdvisor review summary, Riccardo Cooking Class — Pasta Class and Sauces (5.0★ · 536 reviews), 2025

redditQuotes.text: Boasts 5 stars across all platforms with hundreds of glowing reviews… the chef's ability to simplify complex techniques makes the class accessible and enjoyable.
redditQuotes.source: — Girl With Blue Sails '5 Top Pasta Making Classes in Rome', published 2024

places.name: Pastamania in Rome
places.neighborhood: Centro Storico (Palazzo Grazioli, between Pantheon and Piazza Venezia)
places.whatToOrder: The single Pasta Making class is the only class — you don't need to choose. Wine, dessert, and limoncello are all included.
places.insiderTip: The entrance is genuinely hard to find — don't walk into the main palazzo entrance, go around to the back corner of Via della Gatta. Lunch slot is the move if you want to keep your evening free for dinner.
places.editorialSummary: Capped at 10 people, in a hidden entrance inside Palazzo Grazioli (yes, the same palazzo Berlusconi used to live in), and located literally three minutes from the Pantheon. You make ravioli, tortelli, and fettuccine in 3 hours, sit at a long communal table, drink organic Tuscan wine, and finish with limoncello shots. The 4.9★ / 5.0★ ratings are real and consistent.

redditQuotes.text: With a maximum of 10 travelers per session, everyone gets a chance to roll dough, shape pasta, and ask questions without feeling lost in a crowd. The guides are praised for their know-how and approachable teaching style.
redditQuotes.source: — TripAdvisor review summary, Pastamania in Rome (4.9★ · 90 reviews), 2025

redditQuotes.text: Reviewers frequently mention the generous portions and quality of food, with some stating it's the best pasta they ate throughout their travels.
redditQuotes.source: — TripAdvisor Travelers' Choice listing for Pastamania, 2025

places.name: Cesarine — Home Cooking Class with a Local in Rome
places.neighborhood: Various (host's home; centro storico, Prati, or Monti depending on Cesarina)
places.address: Address provided after booking; coordinator: Cesarine srl, Bologna HQ — Rome network operates citywide
places.priceRange: €80–€189 · 3–6 hours (incl. market visit on premium tier)
places.whatToOrder: If your budget allows, book the 'Cooking class with market visit and 3 recipes' (€189, ~6 hours) — you walk Campo de' Fiori with your host first, then cook. The standard 3-hour home class at ~€85 is the better entry point.
places.insiderTip: You only get the host's exact address after booking, and matching is done by Cesarine's team — message them in advance if you have a strong preference (Trastevere, near a metro stop, etc.) and they'll do their best.
places.editorialSummary: Cesarine is Italy's oldest network of home cooks (founded 2004) and the most trusted way to actually cook in a stranger's apartment without the experience feeling staged. You're paired with a 'Cesarina' (a vetted Roman home cook), she walks you through three traditional recipes from her family — typically a starter, fresh pasta, and a dessert — and you eat together with wine. The premium tier includes a Campo de' Fiori market visit before the class.

redditQuotes.text: We really enjoyed our cooking class with Maria and Giorgio. We learned to make several pasta dishes that we will be able to share with our family.
redditQuotes.source: — TripAdvisor review, Cesarine Home Cooking Class in Rome (4.9★ · 22 reviews), posted Mar 2025

redditQuotes.text: Our cooking class in Rome with Valeria and Valentina was the best! My teenage son and I took this class together and we thoroughly enjoyed it.
redditQuotes.source: — TripAdvisor review, Cesarine Home Cooking Class in Rome, posted Jun 2025

places.name: Cook With Mamma
places.neighborhood: Aurelio (just west of the Vatican / Trastevere edge)
places.whatToOrder: The 'Much More Than a Cooking Class' (~€95, 3–4h) is the standard adult class. The Family Pasta + Tiramisu version is purpose-built for kids and explicitly priced for families.
places.insiderTip: Email Fiamma directly through the site if you want the wine pairing add-on — she's a working sommelier and the wines are markedly better than what's bundled into most cooking classes. Vegetarian and pescatarian dietary needs are easy.
places.editorialSummary: A genuinely family-run class — Mamma Debora cooks, daughter Fiamma is the sommelier, the son helps with logistics, and the dog (Rolly) watches. It's hosted in their actual Roman apartment, not a commercial kitchen, and the second 'Kitchen of Mamma' location near Termini lets you add a Mercato Esquilino market visit. Reviews consistently say it feels like being adopted by a Roman family for an afternoon.

redditQuotes.text: Cook with Mamma exceeded expectations in terms of being informative, entertaining, and serving really good pasta & tiramisu, with Mamma's personable approach making it a memorable experience.
redditQuotes.source: — TripAdvisor review summary, Cook With Mamma (5.0★ · 23 reviews), 2025

redditQuotes.text: The class is held in someone's home rather than a restaurant and runs like guests are friends or family.
redditQuotes.source: — TripAdvisor review, Cook With Mamma, posted 2024

places.name: Holy Pizza
places.neighborhood: Borgo (between Vatican Museums and Castel Sant'Angelo)
places.whatToOrder: Holy Pizza! Roman Pizza & Gelato Class — you make Roman thin-crust pizza in a domestic oven (technique you can replicate at home), eat antipasto while it bakes, and finish with gelato. Wine and beer included.
places.insiderTip: Pair it with a morning Vatican Museums visit — the kitchen is literally a 6-minute walk from the museum exit. The space is air-conditioned, which matters in July and August when most cooking schools are sweltering.
places.editorialSummary: Rome's best-rated pizza-focused class (5.0★ / 604 reviews, ranked #9 of 362 Rome workshops) and the only major class that's both genuinely about pizza and actually in a UNESCO-listed historic loft a 5-minute walk from the Vatican Museums. Capped at 8 people. Includes a homemade gelato demo at the end.

redditQuotes.text: This was a special, fun and enriching experience in Rome… The host/chef was delightful, funny and inclusive of everyone.
redditQuotes.source: — Melanie J., TripAdvisor review for Holy Pizza, posted Jul 2023

redditQuotes.text: We had a fabulous time! I took my 12 and 15 year old and they said it was their favorite experience in Rome!
redditQuotes.source: — Laura T., TripAdvisor review for Holy Pizza, posted Nov 2023

places.name: Walks of Italy — Pasta & Gelato Making in Trastevere
places.address: Meeting point: Piazza Trilussa, Trastevere (kitchen 2 min walk away on Via di Santa Maria dell'Anima nearby)
places.whatToOrder: The single Pasta Making Class with Gelato & Wine is what you book — there's no decision tree. They run a separate Trastevere food tour you can stack the next day.
places.insiderTip: This is the right pick if you're not comfortable navigating an unmarked Roman doorbell — meeting at Piazza Trilussa is impossible to miss. Vegetarian works fine; vegan is harder (the fresh pasta uses egg).
places.editorialSummary: The most reliably-booked Trastevere class for travelers who want a brand-name operator with English-speaking staff and crystal-clear logistics. You make fettuccine and ravioli from scratch in a small modern kitchen two minutes from Piazza Trilussa, then watch a live gelato demo and eat everything with prosecco and wine. Group max is 14, meeting point is dead simple, and the chef rotation (Luca, Frederica, Gianmaria) gets consistently strong reviews.

redditQuotes.text: Recent verified reviews praise instructors like Luca and Frederica as excellent, noting the class was as informative as it was fun with very high quality food and wine. Luca and Gianmaria are incredible people and amazing chefs.
redditQuotes.source: — TripAdvisor review summary, Walks of Italy Rome Pasta-Making Class, 2024

redditQuotes.text: Eating Europe's Trastevere pasta-making class where chef Toni was super engaging and travelers learned a lot.
redditQuotes.source: — LiamTheTraveller, Rick Steves Italy travel forum, posted Mar 2025 (referring to the same Trastevere pasta-class scene)
